ranked_hypotheses.hypothesis: The associative path is optimization-misaligned or poorly conditioned for the pairwise ranking objective.
supporting_evidence: On the independent corpus, associative Hit@1 rises only from 0.0222 at 0 updates to 0.1222 at 240, while direct reaches 0.8861.
Associative MRR rises from 0.1599 to 0.2446, showing learning but slow and insufficient improvement.

Direct ranking exposes the query-evidence bilinear interaction directly; associative scoring requires query projection, memory projections, attention, slots, and score-head composition before the ranking signal reaches the relevant evidence.
contradictory_evidence: Associative gradients and parameter mutations were finite and telemetry passed.
Associative performance improved monotonically at the reported independent milestones, so the path is not completely nonfunctional.
ranked_hypotheses.minimal_experiment: Read-only gradient/Jacobian attribution on a fixed small sample, followed only if separately authorized by a one-variable optimization comparison using the existing architecture and objective.
ranked_hypotheses.expected_observable: Large attenuation or disagreement between direct ranking gradients and gradients reaching associative score-connected tensors; or markedly slower loss reduction under matched updates.
ranked_hypotheses.resources: Read-only attribution should fit existing NumPy/FP32 limits; any training follow-up must remain one thread, one subprocess, RSS <= 256 MiB.
ranked_hypotheses.scientific_risk: Changing objective or optimizer can confound architecture and optimization explanations.
ranked_hypotheses.falsifier: If associative and direct paths show comparable gradient alignment, conditioning, and loss reduction on matched examples, this hypothesis loses priority.

ranked_hypotheses.hypothesis: The associative bottleneck and slot-attention representation do not preserve evidence distinctions needed by the scoring head.
supporting_evidence: Independent final associative attention is close to uniform relative to uniform baselines; required-evidence attention is not consistently enriched.
Slot cosine similarities remain substantial, indicating limited slot diversity rather than strongly specialized evidence slots.

The associative model improves on the larger corpus but remains weak on the independent corpus, consistent with a representation that can fit a structured shortcut without robust evidence discrimination.
contradictory_evidence: Query sensitivity is nonzero, so the representation is not fully query-insensitive.
Associative Complete@5 reaches 1.0 on the larger development-validation corpus, showing that the architecture can express a successful ranking on that distribution.
ranked_hypotheses.minimal_experiment: Read-only probe of per-evidence latent separability, slot assignment entropy, required-versus-nonrequired score margins, and representation linear separability using existing checkpoints.
ranked_hypotheses.expected_observable: Low required-evidence margin, low slot specialization, and weak separability despite nonzero query sensitivity.
ranked_hypotheses.resources: CPU/NumPy analysis only; no new weights or dependencies.
ranked_hypotheses.scientific_risk: Post-hoc probes can describe failure without identifying whether the cause is architecture or training.
ranked_hypotheses.falsifier: Strong evidence-specific margins and separable latent representations with poor ranking would shift priority back to the objective or score head.

ranked_hypotheses.hypothesis: The larger validation corpus contains a shortcut or ceiling that inflates associative Complete@5 and is not a reliable generalization measure.
supporting_evidence: Associative Complete@5 progresses from 0.5806 at initialization to 1.0 at 240 on the larger corpus, while independent Complete@5 is only 0.1333.
The larger corpus has a reported 100% Complete@5 ceiling at both collection sizes 64 and 128.
The independent corpus was explicitly separated because it has different construction and no expected-abstention examples.
contradictory_evidence: The larger corpus is a documented development-validation artifact rather than an undocumented test set.
The same associative checkpoint does not obtain uniformly high scores on the independent corpus.
ranked_hypotheses.minimal_experiment: Read-only audit of evidence identity overlap, template relationships, query-to-record lexical/embedding shortcuts, and per-scenario required-evidence composition between the larger corpus and training data.
ranked_hypotheses.expected_observable: Identity/template leakage, easier positive separation, or construction-dependent evidence ordering in the larger corpus.
ranked_hypotheses.resources: Offline JSON/NumPy analysis; no protected holdout access.
ranked_hypotheses.scientific_risk: Calling it leakage without an identity audit would overstate the evidence.
ranked_hypotheses.falsifier: A clean identity and shortcut audit plus matched difficulty distributions would reduce this hypothesis to ordinary distribution shift.

ranked_hypotheses.hypothesis: Direct ranking benefits from a simpler, less bottlenecked query-evidence interaction rather than a special initialization advantage.
supporting_evidence: Direct final independent Hit@1 is 0.8861 versus associative 0.1222.
Direct final independent Complete@5 is 0.3361 versus associative 0.1333.
The direct final result is stable under the evaluated evidence-order reversal, while the direct zero-initialized control is order-sensitive only because of ties.
contradictory_evidence: The direct model has only one bilinear parameter matrix and therefore is not capacity-matched in functional path complexity to the associative model.
The zero direct control demonstrates that tie behavior can dominate some initial measurements.
ranked_hypotheses.minimal_experiment: A frozen, read-only score decomposition comparing direct bilinear scores with associative score-head inputs and margins; any new trained control must be separately authorized.
ranked_hypotheses.expected_observable: Direct margins remain large before the associative score head while associative latent-to-score margins remain compressed.
ranked_hypotheses.scientific_risk: A new direct control could win simply because it is easier, not because it is a better memory architecture.
ranked_hypotheses.falsifier: If associative pre-score evidence margins are strong and only the final score head loses them, the direct advantage is localized rather than end-to-end.

ranked_hypotheses.hypothesis: Evidence order, normalized-template collisions, or candidate construction create residual evaluation confounding.
supporting_evidence: The direct zero initialization changes independent Hit@1 from 1.0 to 0.0 under reversal with 360 tied rows.
Six normalized-template collision groups were identified.
The independent corpus has no expected-abstention examples, limiting evaluation of rejection behavior.
contradictory_evidence: Final associative aggregate metrics are unchanged under the evaluated reversal.
Final direct aggregate metrics are unchanged under the evaluated reversal, apart from six tie rows.
ranked_hypotheses.minimal_experiment: Read-only stratified evaluation across collision groups, candidate permutations, required-evidence counts, and scenario categories.
ranked_hypotheses.expected_observable: If confounding is material, effects will concentrate in collision or tie strata rather than appear uniformly.
ranked_hypotheses.scientific_risk: Permutation tests can become multiple-comparison exercises without predeclared summaries.
ranked_hypotheses.falsifier: Stable stratified results after removing collision groups would demote this hypothesis.

overall_assessment: The evidence supports a multi-factor explanation led by optimization/path conditioning and an associative representation bottleneck, with a separate high-confidence limitation in the larger validation corpus. Existing evidence cannot uniquely identify one root cause without new controlled probes.
